vision.name: IsoForge
vision.tagline: Describe it. Watch it build. Ship the cube.
vision.description: IsoForge is a local-first CLI and web-preview tool that lets developers generate isometric cube-art logos through conversation. Instead of generating unpredictable pixel images, an LLM agent edits a strict, typed JSON scene graph (the IsoDSL) representing shapes on a 1x1x1 isometric grid. A deterministic render engine paints that JSON into a live-updating local web preview, giving users reproducible, diffable, versionable logo designs they can iterate on conversationally and export as SVG, PNG, or full app-icon sets.
goals: Enable fast, high-quality logo/icon generation for dev tools, repos, and internal apps without hiring a designer
Replace unpredictable diffusion-based image generation with a structured, deterministic design pipeline
Make design iteration conversational — chat is the editor, not a separate mode
Provide full version history, diffing, undo, and revert for design iterations
Support portable, shareable, agent-readable design artifacts (themes and scenes as JSON)
Deliver a frictionless local-only tool experience with no accounts or cloud dependency
Offer a complete export pipeline covering SVG, PNG, and full app-icon bundles
target_users: Software developers needing quick logos for GitHub repos or CLI tools
Indie hackers and solo founders building SaaS products
Internal tools builders needing icons for dashboards or bots
Dev teams wanting consistent, on-brand placeholder or production icons
Designers/technical users who want an editable, reproducible design source of truth
vision.problem_statement: Dev teams and indie builders frequently need clean, professional-looking logos or icons quickly, but hiring a designer is overkill and generic AI image generators produce unpredictable, non-editable outputs that don't fit technical brand aesthetics. There's no fast, iterative, structured way to generate the isometric cube-art style that has become the visual standard for dev tools and SaaS products.
success_metrics: Time from CLI launch to exported final logo
Number of chat iterations needed to reach a satisfactory design
Adoption rate (pipx installs / active CLI sessions)
Percentage of sessions ending in successful export
Reuse rate of saved themes and reimported .isoforge.json scenes
User retention across multiple design sessions/projects
Volume and diversity of exported formats (SVG/PNG/app-icon bundles) used

db_schema.raw_sql:
-- IsoForge full schema migration

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;

-- ============================================================
-- scene_store: projects
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE projects (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    current_scene_version_id UUID,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_projects_created_at ON projects (created_at);

-- ============================================================
-- agent_orchestrator: conversations
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE conversations (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    project_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES projects (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    title TEXT,
    model_provider TEXT,
    model_name TEXT,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_conversations_project_id ON conversations (project_id);

-- ============================================================
-- scene_store: scene_versions (created before messages due to FK from messages)
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE scene_versions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    project_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES projects (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    conversation_id UUID REFERENCES conversations (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    parent_version_id UUID REFERENCES scene_versions (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    version_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
    scene_json JSONB NOT NULL,
    patch_json JSONB,
    change_summary TEXT,
    created_by TEXT,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_scene_versions_project_id ON scene_versions (project_id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_scene_versions_project_version_number ON scene_versions (project_id, version_number);
CREATE INDEX idx_scene_versions_conversation_id ON scene_versions (conversation_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_scene_versions_parent_version_id ON scene_versions (parent_version_id);

-- Now that scene_versions exists, add FK from projects.current_scene_version_id
ALTER TABLE projects
    ADD CONSTRAINT fk_projects_current_scene_version
    FOREIGN KEY (current_scene_version_id) REFERENCES scene_versions (id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

-- ============================================================
-- agent_orchestrator: messages
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE messages (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    conversation_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES conversations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    role TEXT NOT NULL,
    content TEXT,
    tool_call_payload JSONB,
    resulting_scene_version_id UUID REFERENCES scene_versions (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    sequence_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_messages_conversation_id ON messages (conversation_id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_messages_conversation_seq ON messages (conversation_id, sequence_number);

-- ============================================================
-- scene_store: themes
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE themes (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    is_builtin BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    theme_json JSONB NOT NULL,
    source_project_id UUID REFERENCES projects (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_themes_name ON themes (name);
CREATE INDEX idx_themes_source_project_id ON themes (source_project_id);

-- ============================================================
-- render_engine: render_jobs
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE render_jobs (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    scene_version_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES scene_versions (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    job_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
    error_message TEXT,
    requested_by TEXT,
    started_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_render_jobs_scene_version_id ON render_jobs (scene_version_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_render_jobs_status ON render_jobs (status);

-- ============================================================
-- render_engine: export_artifacts
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE export_artifacts (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    render_job_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES render_jobs (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    artifact_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    file_path TEXT NOT NULL,
    width INTEGER,
    height INTEGER,
    transparent_background BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    metadata_json JSONB,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_export_artifacts_render_job_id ON export_artifacts (render_job_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_export_artifacts_artifact_type ON export_artifacts (artifact_type);

-- ============================================================
-- iso_gateway: api_sessions
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE api_sessions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    project_id UUID REFERENCES projects (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    session_token TEXT NOT NULL,
    client_type TEXT,
    last_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_api_sessions_project_id ON api_sessions (project_id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_api_sessions_session_token ON api_sessions (session_token);

-- ============================================================
-- iso_gateway: websocket_events
-- ============================================================
CREATE TABLE websocket_events (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    session_id UUID REFERENCES api_sessions (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    scene_version_id UUID REFERENCES scene_versions (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    payload_json JSONB,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_websocket_events_session_id ON websocket_events (session_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_websocket_events_scene_version_id ON websocket_events (scene_version_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_websocket_events_created_at ON websocket_events (created_at);

pages.name: Home / Session Launcher
pages.description: Landing view when IsoForge web UI opens with no active session. Shows recent sessions/conversations as resumable cards (thumbnail of last rendered scene, last message preview, timestamp), a prominent 'New Session' CTA, and quick-start templates (blank grid, curated palette starters). Mirrors CLI's 'isoforge chat' entry point for users who prefer clicking over typing commands.

components.name: SessionCard
components.description: Resumable session preview card showing thumbnail render, last message snippet, relative timestamp, and quick actions (resume, delete, duplicate).

components.name: NewSessionDialog

components.name: TemplateGallery
components.description: Grid of curated starter scenes (grid size + palette presets) users can launch a session from directly.

pages.name: Workbench
pages.description: The core three-pane experience: left rail (sessions/themes), center chat transcript with inline DSL diffs, right pane live isometric SVG preview with version filmstrip below it. This is where 95% of user time is spent — chat drives scene mutation, preview hot-reloads via WebSocket in real time.

components.name: SessionRail
components.description: Left sidebar listing active/recent sessions and saved themes, collapsible, with Cmd+K command palette trigger.

components.name: ChatTranscript
components.description: Scrollable message history rendering user turns and agent turns; agent turns show a summary of the scene patch applied plus a collapsible JSON diff viewer.

components.name: ChatMessageBubble

components.name: DSLDiffViewer

components.name: ChatInputBar
components.description: Primary input for conversing with the LLM agent; supports multiline, slash-commands (/theme, /revert, /export), and send-on-enter.

components.name: IsoPreviewCanvas
components.description: Live SVG isometric renderer with pan/zoom, background toggle (transparent checkerboard vs solid), and pulse animation on hot-reload updates from WebSocket.

components.name: PreviewToolbar
components.description: Floating toolbar over the preview canvas: zoom controls, background toggle, fullscreen, open export modal, open JSON inspector drawer.

components.name: VersionFilmstrip
components.description: Horizontal scrollable strip of thumbnail renders representing scene version history; click to preview, right-click for context menu (revert, diff, branch).

components.name: SceneInspectorDrawer
components.description: Collapsible drawer showing the raw, read-only syntax-highlighted current IsoDSL JSON with copy button and validation status badge.

components.name: ValidationBadge
components.description: Small status pill showing whether the current scene passes schema validation, with hover detail on errors.

components.name: CommandPalette
components.description: Cmd+K global palette to switch sessions, apply themes, trigger export, or run slash-command equivalents without typing in chat.

pages.name: Version History Explorer
pages.description: Full-page deep-dive into a session's version graph when the filmstrip isn't enough — for comparing distant versions, viewing full diff chains, and branching. Includes a git-log-style commit graph visualization.

components.name: VersionGraph
components.description: Vertical commit-graph-style visualization of scene versions with branch points, linked to conversation turns.

components.name: VersionCompareView
components.description: Side-by-side rendered preview + JSON diff for two selected versions.

components.name: DSLDiffViewer
components.description: Reused diff viewer component for comparing two arbitrary versions' JSON.

pages.name: Theme & Palette Manager
pages.description: Library of built-in curated palettes plus user-saved custom themes. Users can preview a palette applied to a sample scene, edit theme JSON, save/import/export theme files, and lock a theme to a session so the LLM respects constrained colors while iterating.

components.name: PaletteCard

components.name: ThemeEditorDialog
components.description: Modal for creating/editing a custom theme's color faces and metadata, with live preview cube.

components.name: ThemeImportDropzone

components.name: IsoPreviewCanvas

pages.name: Export Configuration

shared_components.name: IsoPreviewCanvas

frontend.design_notes:
IsoForge's web UI is the "cockpit" for a local design tool — it should feel like a hybrid of a chat app, a code editor, and a design tool preview pane (think: Linear's chat-adjacent polish + Figma's canvas confidence + a terminal's density). This is NOT a marketing-style SaaS app; it's a single-user localhost tool that opens the moment you run `isoforge chat`, so it should feel instant, keyboard-driven, and "developer home turf" — dark-mode-first, monospace accents for JSON/DSL bits, but with a genuinely beautiful isometric render as the hero.

Layout: a persistent three-pane workbench (not a multi-page marketing flow). Left rail = session/conversation list + theme/palette manager. Center = chat transcript styled like a technical pairing session (user bubbles vs. agent bubbles that render inline diffs of the IsoDSL JSON, collapsible). Right pane = the live SVG isometric preview canvas, pinned and always visible, with a floating toolbar for zoom/pan/background-toggle/export. This mirrors the backend's mental model exactly: conversation turns → scene patches → rendered preview, so the UI should visually show that causal chain (small "diff applied" toast animations pulsing the right-pane preview on update).

Key interaction principle: the chat input is the primary design tool — no separate "properties panel" for manually editing shapes in v1 (that's the LLM's job), but we DO surface a read-only, syntax-highlighted JSON inspector (collapsible drawer) for power users who want to see/copy the raw IsoDSL, plus a "validate scene" indicator badge. Version history is a horizontal filmstrip of thumbnail renders beneath the preview (like a git commit graph crossed with a film reel) — click any version to preview it, right-click to revert/diff/branch.

Visual language: dark charcoal (#0B0E14) canvas background with a subtle isometric grid watermark pattern, accent gradients pulled dynamically from the active palette/theme (so the UI chrome itself shifts subtly toward teal/purple/sunset-glass tones based on what you're designing — a nice touch of "the tool reflects your creation"). Typography: Inter for UI, JetBrains Mono for JSON/DSL/CLI-echo text. Use shadcn/ui + Radix primitives for command palette (Cmd+K to switch sessions/themes fast, very CLI-native crossover), dialogs (export config), tooltips, and toasts. Framer Motion for the hot-reload pulse animation on preview updates and filmstrip transitions. react-query manages all server state (sessions, scenes, history) with WebSocket-driven cache invalidation for true live-reload; zustand handles ephemeral UI state (active drawer, canvas zoom/pan, selected version, theme-preview overrides) that shouldn't round-trip to the server.

Export flow is a dedicated modal (not a page) — because it's a terminal action within a session, not a navigation destination: format tabs (SVG/PNG/App Icon Bundle/.isoforge.json), live-updating size/padding preview using the same renderer component, and a manifest checklist for bundle contents. Keep the whole app feeling like one continuous workbench you never "navigate away" from — sessions are switched via command palette or left rail, not full route changes with jarring reloads, even though React Router backs the URL structure for shareable/bookmarkable session links.
frontend.theme: shadcn/ui + tailwindcss + radix primitives, dark-mode-first with dynamic accent theming from active palette

clients.description: Public entrypoint client for the iso_gateway (Go) service. Handles session lifecycle, chat turns, render/export routing, scene proxying, live preview WebSocket, and static frontend serving. All other backend services are accessed indirectly through this gateway from the browser.

methods.name: health
methods.description: Checks gateway service health. Throws NetworkError if unreachable; resolves with status payload otherwise. Useful for readiness probes and status banners.

methods.name: createSession
methods.description: Starts a new isoforge chat session. Throws ApiError on validation failure (400) or server error (5xx).

methods.name: getSession
methods.description: Fetches session status/details by id. Throws ApiError with status 404 if session not found.

methods.name: endSession
methods.description: Stops/ends an isoforge chat session. Idempotent-ish: throws ApiError 404 if already ended or missing.

methods.name: sendMessage
methods.description: Sends a chat turn to the agent via the gateway, which proxies to agent_orchestrator. Throws ApiError on invalid session or LLM/tool-call failure (returned as 502/500 with details).
methods.typescript_signature: async sendMessage(sessionId: string, req: ChatTurnRequest): Promise<ChatTurnResponse>

methods.name: connectPreviewSocket
methods.description: Opens a WebSocket connection for live scene hot-reload preview. Returns a WebSocket handle wrapper; caller should call `.close()` when done. Reconnection is left to the caller (wrap with retry/backoff as needed). Emits errors via handlers.onError rather than throwing.

methods.name: render

sdk.auth_pattern: Bearer token auth via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, attached automatically by an internal `AuthTokenProvider`. Token is stored in memory only (never localStorage) and set via `client.setAuthToken(token)` or injected at construction via `IsoforgeClientConfig.getToken: () => string | undefined`. Each generated client class accepts a shared `HttpClient` instance that centralizes token attachment, base URL resolution, and 401 handling (triggers an optional `onUnauthorized` callback to allow re-auth flows). All methods throw a typed `ApiError` (with `status`, `code`, `message`, `details`) on non-2xx responses; network failures throw `NetworkError`. Consumers are expected to wrap calls in try/catch or use the provided `safeCall` helper that returns a `Result<T, ApiError>` union for ergonomic error handling without exceptions.
sdk.base_url_config: Single configurable base URL for the iso_gateway service (the sole public entrypoint; other services are proxied through it) set via `IsoforgeClientConfig.baseUrl` (defaults to `window.location.origin` in browser or `process.env.ISOFORGE_API_URL` in Node). WebSocket URL is derived automatically by swapping `http(s)` for `ws(s)` on the base URL, or can be overridden via `wsBaseUrl`. All client classes share this config through a root `IsoforgeSDK` factory: `new IsoforgeSDK({ baseUrl, getToken })` which instantiates and exposes each service client.

adrs.title: Adopt a typed IsoDSL JSON scene graph as the single source of truth, edited via LLM function-calling
adrs.context: IsoForge must guarantee reproducible, diffable, versionable logo designs rather than unpredictable diffusion output. The LLM needs a way to both create and incrementally patch a design without freeform text parsing errors.
adrs.decision: The agent_orchestrator will interact with the LLM exclusively via structured function/tool-calling (e.g. `set_scene`, `patch_scene`) whose arguments are validated against the IsoDSL JSON Schema before being accepted. No raw LLM text is ever parsed as design data; only tool-call payloads are trusted. Every accepted mutation produces a new immutable scene version.
adrs.rationale: Structured tool-calling eliminates ambiguous natural-language parsing, enforces the 1x1x1 grid constraint at the schema level, and makes every LLM turn a well-typed, testable operation. This is the core differentiator of the product (structured, not stochastic) and must be enforced architecturally, not just by prompting.
consequences: Requires maintaining a versioned JSON Schema for IsoDSL shared between agent_orchestrator, render_engine, and scene_store.
LLM providers must support function-calling (OpenAI/Anthropic) or an equivalent constrained-output shim for local models via Ollama.
Enables free undo/diff/version history since every state is a validated, serializable document.
Adds validation-and-rejection round-trip latency when the LLM proposes an invalid patch (must re-prompt or auto-correct).

adrs.title: Single-user local-first deployment with iso_gateway as the sole coordination point
adrs.context: IsoForge is a local developer tool (like `npm run dev`), not a hosted multi-tenant SaaS. There are no user accounts, and the CLI, browser preview, agent, renderer, and store all run on the same machine.
adrs.decision: iso_gateway (Go) will run as a single local process exposing a REST + WebSocket API on localhost, acting as the only entry point the CLI and React preview UI talk to. It internally proxies/coordinates calls to agent_orchestrator, render_engine, and scene_store, which are treated as local backend processes/sidecars, not independently network-exposed services.
adrs.rationale: A single gateway process simplifies the local topology, avoids the need for auth/multi-tenancy infrastructure, and gives one place to implement WebSocket fan-out for live scene updates to the browser. Go was chosen for the gateway for low-overhead concurrency (goroutines per WS connection) and a single static binary that's easy to bundle alongside the Python tool.
consequences: No cloud accounts or multi-tenant auth needed initially, reducing scope significantly.

iso_gateway becomes a critical single point of failure for the local session; it must be resilient to backend process crashes (e.g. render_engine dying mid-export) and report errors gracefully to the CLI/UI.
Binding to localhost only is sufficient for v1; any future multi-device/remote-collab feature would require revisiting auth and network exposure.
Packaging must ship/orchestrate four separate runtimes (Go binary x2, Python service x2) which pipx/PyInstaller packaging needs to account for (likely via subprocess management from the CLI).

adrs.title: SQLite + JSON files for local persistence of scene history, themes, and palettes
adrs.context: scene_store must persist version history, diffs, themes, and palettes fully locally with zero setup, while also keeping designs git-friendly and human-portable (`.isoforge.json` export/import, theme JSON sharing).
adrs.decision: scene_store (Go) will use SQLite as the system of record for version metadata, conversation-linked history, and diff indexing, while the canonical IsoDSL scene documents and theme/palette definitions are stored as standalone JSON files on disk that SQLite rows reference by path/hash.
adrs.rationale: SQLite gives zero-setup relational querying for history/diff operations (`isoforge history`, `isoforge diff v3 v4`) without a server process. Keeping the actual scene/theme content as plain JSON files (rather than blobs in SQLite) preserves the 'portable, git-friendly, agent-readable' requirement and makes `.isoforge.json` export trivial (it's already a file).
consequences: Every scene version is both a DB row (for querying/ordering/diffing) and a JSON file on disk (for portability) - scene_store must keep these in sync transactionally.
Enables trivial `isoforge revert vN` (just re-point current pointer) and `isoforge diff v3 v4` (structural JSON diff) without re-deriving state.
No built-in multi-machine sync; users needing backup/sharing rely on git or manual file copying of the project directory.
Concurrent writes are not a concern in v1 given single-user local usage, simplifying locking logic.

adrs.title: Deterministic server-side rendering/export pipeline separate from the live preview renderer
adrs.context: The React/SVG preview in the browser needs fast, interactive hot-reload rendering, but final export (SVG/PNG/app-icon bundles) must be pixel-exact, scriptable, reproducible, and independent of any particular browser's rendering quirks.
adrs.decision: render_engine (Python) owns the canonical, deterministic transform from IsoDSL JSON to output artifacts using svgwrite for SVG generation and cairosvg/resvg for PNG rasterization and icon bundle assembly. The React preview implements its own lightweight SVG projection renderer for live hot-reload display, but is never used as the source of exported files - all `export` commands always go through render_engine via iso_gateway.
adrs.rationale: Separating 'live interactive preview' from 'canonical export' avoids coupling exports to browser DOM/canvas quirks (fonts, anti-aliasing, headless-browser dependencies) and keeps exports scriptable/CI-friendly and guaranteed deterministic (same JSON always produces the same file bytes). It does mean two SVG-projection implementations must stay visually consistent.
consequences: Two independent isometric-projection implementations (TS in the browser, Python in render_engine) must be kept in sync via shared test fixtures/golden images to avoid preview/export visual drift.
Exports have no runtime browser dependency, making app-icon bundle generation fast and CI/headless-friendly.
Adds a small maintenance cost of a shared 'golden scene -> expected output' test suite spanning both languages.
PNG rasterization quality/behavior is pinned to cairosvg/resvg versions, which must be version-locked for reproducibility guarantees.

adrs.title: Pluggable LLM backend (hosted function-calling APIs or local Ollama) behind a single agent interface
adrs.context: IsoForge wants to support both hosted LLMs (OpenAI/Anthropic function-calling) for best quality and local models via Ollama for privacy/offline use, without duplicating the IsoDSL editing logic per provider.
adrs.decision: agent_orchestrator defines a single internal `AgentBackend` interface (propose_scene, patch_scene, tool schema definitions) with concrete adapters for OpenAI/Anthropic native function-calling and an Ollama-based adapter that emulates tool-calling via constrained prompting + JSON-schema validation/retry. The backend is selected via CLI config (`isoforge chat --model ...`) and is invisible to iso_gateway and scene_store.
adrs.rationale: Isolating provider-specific quirks behind one interface lets the product support offline/local usage (a stated value: local-first, no accounts) while still defaulting to higher-quality hosted models, without forking core conversation/versioning logic.
consequences: Ollama/local-model path requires extra validation-and-repair logic since it lacks native structured tool-calling guarantees, increasing latency/complexity for that backend.
New model providers can be added by implementing one adapter interface without touching iso_gateway, scene_store, or render_engine.
Quality/consistency of scene edits may vary noticeably between hosted and local backends; this must be documented for users.
Requires agent_orchestrator to own retry/backoff and schema-repair logic centrally rather than per-provider.

architecture.system_diagram_description: A single local machine hosts four cooperating processes launched by the IsoForge CLI. The developer interacts via the CLI (Python/Typer) and/or a browser-based React preview at localhost:4747. Both clients communicate exclusively with iso_gateway (Go), which exposes REST endpoints for commands (chat turn, export, history, revert, diff) and a WebSocket hub that pushes live scene updates to the React preview whenever the scene changes. iso_gateway routes chat requests to agent_orchestrator (Python), which talks to a pluggable LLM backend (OpenAI/Anthropic function-calling or local Ollama) and returns a validated IsoDSL JSON scene or patch. iso_gateway sends the resulting scene to scene_store (Go) to persist a new immutable version (SQLite metadata + JSON file on disk for the scene/theme content) and to compute diffs/history. iso_gateway also broadcasts the updated scene over WebSocket to the React preview, which renders it client-side using its own lightweight SVG isometric projection for instant hot-reload feedback. When the user issues an export command, iso_gateway forwards the current validated scene to render_engine (Python), which deterministically produces SVG, PNG, or full app-icon bundle files using svgwrite and cairosvg/resvg, writing results to the local exports directory and returning status through iso_gateway back to the CLI/UI. All four services run locally with no external network exposure beyond calls to the chosen LLM provider API when a hosted backend is selected.

infrastructure.deployment_target: Local developer machine (single-user desktop CLI tool) - no cloud deployment required; distributed as a pipx-installable Python package that subprocess-manages local Go binaries, with all services communicating over localhost
suggested_managed_services: None required for core functionality (fully local/offline-capable)
Optional: OpenAI API for cloud LLM inference
Optional: Anthropic API for cloud LLM inference
Optional: GitHub Releases or similar for binary distribution/updates
Optional: PyPI for pipx package distribution
infrastructure.scaling_notes: This is a single-user, local-first desktop tool with no multi-tenant or horizontal scaling requirements. Each service instance runs as a lightweight local process per user session. iso_gateway's WebSocket concurrency model (Go) comfortably handles a single browser preview client. scene_store's SQLite usage is appropriate given single-writer, low-concurrency local access. The main scaling consideration is startup/teardown latency of subprocess-managed binaries and ensuring clean port allocation when multiple CLI instances run concurrently on one machine. If a future multi-user/hosted mode is desired, iso_gateway and agent_orchestrator would need session isolation, and SQLite would need to be swapped for a networked database.
